filename: Reduced Order Modeling for Linearized Representations of Microphysical Process Rates.pdf
title: Reduced Order Modeling for Linearized Representations of Microphysical Process Rates
parameterization_target: droplet collision-coalescence rate and droplet size distribution evolution
testbed_rationale: The 16 simulation cases generated by the 1D kinematic driver model with TAU bin microphysics are publicly available on Zenodo with open PyTorch code on GitHub, providing an ideal benchmark for evaluating reduced-order modeling and parameterization of collision-coalescence.
pain_points: Latent variable representations are not conserved quantities, creating difficulties for spatial advection and diffusion in 3D host atmospheric models
Neglects turbulent enhancement of droplet collision-coalescence and air density variations
Stochasticity of collision-coalescence is ignored due to deterministic bin microphysics kinetic collection solving
1D column simulations do not capture 3D cloud dynamics, turbulent transport, and mixing effects like eddy hopping
extraction_notes: The preprint was submitted to JAMES. An autoencoder is first used with intrinsic dimension estimators to establish that collision-coalescence has an intrinsic dimension of ~3, followed by a Koopman-inspired VAE architecture with nlat = 3 that globally linearizes collision-coalescence.
